scope: macOS real security adapter with disposable synthetic settings and previously absent credential accounts; no existing user credential is changed.
identity: Setting name, colon and first 16 hexadecimal SHA256 characters of the same lexical absolute temporary configuration path, matching the frozen baseline.
sequence: Verify all three synthetic-path accounts are absent before performing any writes; stop on unexpected lookup results.
Native CLI migrates the synthetic file credential to Keychain; verify exact account/password read-back and no plaintext in the saved file or command output.
Frozen Node CLI reads the same configuration, then updates the same synthetic account through stdin; verify exact read-back.
Native CLI reads the updated account and migrates back to file; verify credential preservation, private file mode and Keychain deletion.
Frozen Node migrates to Keychain again; native CLI unsets the synthetic credential and verifies deletion.
Finally remove only the exact accounts proven absent before this run and verify absence, then remove the disposable directory. Retain bounded metadata-only results.
policy: Honor the real system policy. Do not bypass allowlists/locks or unlock a user Keychain. An interactive/permission/unavailable result remains failed or blocked evidence.
acceptance: All sequence assertions and cleanup pass against exact native/frozen source identities. This host check does not qualify other macOS versions, GUI consent flows, all failure/rollback cases, real user secrets or publication.
privacy: Synthetic values only; secrets passed through stdin and never retained in reports. Outputs are checked for canaries before any metadata is saved. Existing caller environment configuration/secret overrides are removed only from the synthetic child environment; no shell profile or persistent user settings are edited.
